title: Normalized strict compactification scalar data
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its valuation ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $b,o$ be the simultaneous strict-system section presentation and geometric operations [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For every scheme $T$, fix the abelian coefficient-tower presentation $D_T$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] and the normalized derived reduction $r_T$ [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized]. Use the completed ring $R_T$, its positive quotient projections, and the functors and normalization predicates of [def-sp-complete-compactification-limit-comparison]. There exist compatible scalar squares $h$, normalized reduction/total-limit presentations $a_T$ and identity-on-sections evaluation comparisons $v_T$. For every compactification $X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow p Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] with $X,Z,Y$ quasi-compact quasi-separated, $\ell$ invertible on their residue fields, and $j$ quasi-compact, there exist ordinary strict-system isomorphisms $U_Xj_{!,R}^{\rm Tow}\simeq j_{!,\bullet}U_Z$ and $U_Zp_{*,R}^{\rm Tow}\simeq p_{*,\bullet}U_Y$ whose evaluations are the specified finite scalar comparisons, and a derived isomorphism $U_ZRp_{*,R}^{\rm Tow}\simeq Rp_{*,\bullet}U_Y$ satisfying IsPushScalarNormalized for that ordinary comparison. The unit-projection, tensor-generator, derived-counit and section equations are exactly those in LimitPresentation and Evaluation. This assertion concerns scalar comparisons before taking the compactification limit; it asserts neither invertibility of open/limit nor any compactification image realization.

proof.text: Put $N=r_XM$, and let $U_T$ denote exact restriction of the entire coefficient system to a strict tower of $R_T$-modules. Write $\mathcal L_T$ for total derived limit on those fixed-ring towers, so $L_T=\mathcal L_TU_T$. The pulled-back coefficient identifications commute with inverse image and with the maps $R_T\to A_{n,T}$: these are the projections from the same pulled-back integral coefficient ring. For the open, the slice-site identification therefore gives $j^*R_{\bar X}=R_X$ and $j^*A_{n,\bar X}=A_{n,X}$. The reduction/limit adjunction identifies its unit with the specified quotient augmentation; in particular, writing $q_n:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{n,X}N_n$, we have $\pi_n\eta_M=q_n$. These are actual tower constructions, not a choice of cones for a sequence in a triangulated category.

source.place: Paragraph (2): pulled-back coefficients and the derived-completeness map

proof.text:
On derived coefficient-system categories form the scalar comparisons
$$e_N:j_{!,R}^{\operatorname{Tow}}U_XN\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{\bar X}j_{!,\bullet}N,\qquad d_P:Rp_{*,R}^{\operatorname{Tow}}U_{\bar X}P\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YRp_{*,\bullet}P.$$
For $e$ use the inverse of the ringed open scalar comparison. On extension presheaves it is the identity on each summand; a semilinear transition sends a summand section to its given transition section, so the same identity commutes with every transition. Both sides are exact, hence this identity descends from strict system complexes. For $d$ apply the ring-diagram restriction/direct-image theorem with index $\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, $S_T=R_T$, $B_T=(A_{n,T})_n$, and $a_T=(R_T\to A_{n,T})_n$, taking its inverse. The compatibility square is the one in step 1. Its normalization compares the two factorizations of one ringed-topos map, using the canonical derived composition comparison. Evaluating gives precisely $Rp_{*,R}\operatorname{Res}_{n,\bar X}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{n,Y}Rp_{*,A_n}$, while $e$ gives $j_{!,R}\operatorname{Res}_{n,X}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{n,\bar X}j_{!,A_n}$. Simultaneous system direct images and exact open extension are the stipulated operations, so these are comparisons on systems before evaluation.
